A replica accepted for custody. Created on the basis of {catalogue} by means of {generator}. Layout modelled on {iris}; every number on this page is read from the catalogue, not copied from a screenshot.

There is no Dublin Core record. The catalogue reports this rather than synthesizing metadata from the PDF: this is rule R8 of the iris-dspace skill, never derive metadata from the PDF if a record exists, the flip side of which is that a missing record stays missing.

This is the main entrance, not the library visualizer. The full visualizer of library/ is the grain jbx2, and it is being created separately. This page reproduces the IRIS main page and leads further, rather than becoming a second answer to the same question.

Three paths to one storage unit — that is the point. The catalogue knows this storage unit once; the bytes are available at the original source at WHO, here as a replica page and from a CDN edge server — jsDelivr serves any open repository, so the last path costs this project nothing for hosting. The knowledge graph says what exists and where; the CDN says nothing and simply serves the files.

Where the stored copies actually lie — grain yl5w. The catalogue specifies for each of them the path uploads/<name>.pdf relative to who-iris/, and all three of these paths are absent: #477 moved library/ into this instance and left uploads/ in cat-harness/.
